title: flows.v1
description: The flows control-plane REST surface (flows-api) — the boundary between an MCP/agent client and the reaction engine. Flows are DATA: an ordered list of step names drawn from a fixed vocabulary, plus a trigger event. The API never accepts code, so a wrong step name is a 400 with the vocabulary returned, never a runtime failure. A submitted flow admits a reaction per matching fact; reactions walk their steps and can be steered by audited signals (retry/resume/cancel/wake), never by table surgery. This is a cross-process, independently-deployable boundary (P4): sealed, versioned, golden-pinned.

FlowSubmission.description: POST /flows body — submit a new flow version. `steps` must all be in the live vocabulary or the call is a 400.

name.description: flow name; a resubmission mints the next version

on_event.description: the trigger event type, e.g. meeting.completed

steps.description: ordered step names, all from the vocabulary (GET /flows.steps_vocabulary)

params.description: optional per-flow parameters passed to steps

Flow.description: One flow version as listed by GET /flows. `source` distinguishes an image-baked flow from an API-submitted one.

source.description: image = baked into the deployment; api = submitted via POST /flows

created_by.description: the X-Actor that submitted it (api flows only)

StepDoc.description: One entry of the step vocabulary — a step name and its one-line doc. The vocabulary is the closed set of names a FlowSubmission may use.

FlowList.description: GET /flows response — the vocabulary that bounds submissions, plus every known flow (image + api).

live_within_s.description: seconds until an active flow is live; null for a draft

UnknownSteps.description: POST /flows 400 body — the submission named steps outside the vocabulary. The vocabulary is returned so the caller can self-correct. This is the P4 forcing function: a wrong step is a contract error, not a runtime one.

Reaction.description: One reaction (a fact walking a flow's steps) as listed by GET /reactions. `next_run_at` is the parked wake time — how a scheduled bot dispatch or a blocked step waits at zero cost.

next_run_at.description: epoch seconds of the next scheduled run; null when not parked

SignalResult.description: POST /reactions/{id}/{retry|resume|cancel|wake} response — the applied verb, true. A verb not applicable in the current status is a 409, never a silent no-op.
